steps.text: All of this information is consistent with our hypothesis.
With these data on hand, Rhine Lab's newest results now directly correlate with the ancient Sarkaz legend. I don't think this is an accident.
And if our hypothesis is verified, it will revolutionize everything we know about Originium.
People think that Originium is a source of energy, a calamity; They think it can be used as a weapon, with only narrow applications outside of that. But the truth may be something far greater.

If Originium really 'stores information,' just think about what that implies. From Originium, we will be able to read the story of this world, spanning hundreds or thousands of years, maybe even more...
Does this really not pique your curiosity?

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: I've read all your previous reports already, and agree with your conjecture.

steps.name: Joyce
steps.text: But how can I help you?
You're on board then? That's great news... Thank you so much.
My plan is a bold one...

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: June 18th, clear skies

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: I fell asleep in the cafeteria today. Gummy was worried about me.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: Dr. Silence reminded me that my 'narcolepsy' has gotten worse this month.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: There are more details in my physical examination report.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: The conclusion of the physical: 'Fatigue caused by long-term sleep quality issues.'

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: Dr. Silence said that this was caused by the chip in my brain – Device #9.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: I am aware of these things. I know my own problems much better than those who worry about me, but I still must accept their concern.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: Dr. Silence has advised me to get more rest, which is a measure that I agree with. But what should I do while resting?

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Please continue deploying your pieces.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Ah, there's no need for that.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: This round... is my loss.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Hoo, now that's a rare sight. When's the last time you threw in the towel?

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: I must say... it was a rather long time ago.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: According to the records dating from three hours ago, the current score is one to two.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: In accordance with the best-of-three format, your two wins still makes you the victor of today's match, Rangers.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Gwahaha...

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Ahaha... I suppose that's your way of letting this old man keep some of his dignity.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: No towel visible. Unable to interpret the underlying meaning of this statement.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Girl, you asked me to teach you how to play chess, and I taught you for twenty minutes.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: We played just three games after that. And in the span of those three games, I'm already convinced I can't win anymore.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: That's what it means to throw in the towel.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Understood. Logging of idiom confirmed.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: By the way, Ptilopsis, why'd you suddenly decide to pick up chess? You don't have much free time, right?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Hasn't it been pretty busy in Medical lately?

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Dr. Silence's recommendation. Acquire more hobbies to distract myself.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: So you chose chess?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: And is this really the first time you've played one of these games? You learned way too fast.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Welp, I was thinking I'd want to play a round or two with you, but let's scrap that idea.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Yes, this is my first contact with board games of this type.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Previously, I learned to play different kinds of card and board games from other operators.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Most game sessions were very short in duration.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: I can already guess what happened. They probably all got trounced by the little lady here...

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: I'm not surprised though. Medical is full of bright operators, very accomplished in healing Arts. Chess is probably nothing compared to that stuff.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: If you want more of a challenge, why not try the Doctor? That one's pretty well-versed in all kinds of chess variants. Mighty skilled to boot.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: You'll be waiting around for a long time then... The Doctor would split into three pieces to work that much harder, if it was possible.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Ah, a blunder on my part.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Rangers, will we be concluding today's chess session?

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: What time is it?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Lemme see... Where's my watch?

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: 4:35 in the afternoon. There are three hours until Rangers's scheduled duty. In other words, there are still three hours left until work.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: It's fine, we have plenty of time. Let's have another match then.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: However, one can infer that Rangers may have additional work arrangements today.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Based on the data provided by the Catastrophe Messenger and the Originium particulate matter detection data from the past ten days, one can determine that Rhodes Island may move ahead of schedule today to avoid a potential Catastrophe.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: At that time, it may be necessary to mobilize defenders in advance.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: I've heard the news, same as you, but the Doctor should still be talking things over with the others––

steps.name: Broadcast
steps.text: Attention, all Rhodes Island personnel. Attention, all Rhodes Island personnel.

steps.name: Broadcast
steps.text: In two hours' time, Rhodes Island will conduct evasive maneuvers to avoid a Catastrophe.

steps.name: Broadcast
steps.text: Requesting all personnel inside the ship prepare for the maneuver in advance, in accordance with the staff manual.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Hahaha, guess you were right. That settles it for today's game of chess, then. This old man's got work to do.

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: You amaze me sometimes, Ptilopsis. Just how do you do it...?

steps.name: Noir Corne
steps.text: Don't worry about it, just mumbling to myself. It'd be too rude to ask anyway.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: June 22nd, clear skies

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: I went to see Mayer today to carry out some checks on the operation of Device #9 that I cannot carry out myself.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: Mayer brought up a troubling possibility. I've thought about it before, and have my own expectations.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: In other words, Device #9 has placed an enormous burden on my brain, and while this strain has not increased, my ability to withstand its impact cannot continue at its current level indefinitely.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: Della was a genius. Her accomplishments –– even if flawed –– must be protected.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: Device #9 does have a negative impact on me, and there's also the possibility of it malfunctioning. But had it not stabilized my prior brain disorders, I would not have had the opportunity to express these assessments.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: Furthermore, Della's invention also brought me many functional improvements. Some of these were expected even before the experiment, while others exceeded expectations.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: I can see the flow of Originium particles in the human body, and upon this, my understanding and control of medical Originium Arts have strengthened astoundingly.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: At the time, Della believed that not only was this due to a significant increase in the computational capacity of my brain, but also because of that, I was able to unlock a portion of Originium's functionality as an information pathway.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: That is what Device #9 is.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: Of course, it can have other uses... It can be used as a weapon. It can save people, and it can also bring destruction. Just like Originium itself, except more intuitive to use.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: This is not the outcome that Della wanted.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Gimme a sec... Let's take a look...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: The voltage is stable, and there's nothing wrong with the receiver...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I don't see any problems. Device #9 is working just fine.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Are there any changes in the part that sends requests to read data?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Hrmm....

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Unfortunately, nope.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Are you absolutely positive that Device #9 can output data?

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: That was the designer's original purpose for this device.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: But even after all this time, I still haven't gotten any meaningful data out of it.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: And be honest with me here. You've gotta feel pretty uncomfortable with a chip inside your head, right?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Even the transmission of electronic signals will affect your body to some extent, right? I try to be real careful when remote-controlling my equipment.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: So far, there have been no side effects that influence physiological indicators.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Miss Dellareed really was something else... This project didn't even have the Engineering's blessing. It really is a transcendent invention.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I'm really curious about how this thing was made! Would you happen to have any kind of reference materials? Diagrams, spare parts, anything?

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Negative. There are no backups for Device #9.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Ahh, what a shame.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: But... Joyce...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: All machines are bound to have a service life.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Device #9's design is way too complicated, and I don't just mean the chip itself.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: It's connected to your cerebellum and interacts with a large number of neurons in your brain.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: A single point of failure in any part of the entire system will have catastrophic consequences.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I don't know what you and Miss Dellareed were thinking, but... even for Rhine Lab, this is seriously dangerous.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: ...Biological structures...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I know what you're trying to say.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: 'Biological structures, in essence, are sets of reasonably-working precise machines.' Right?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Seems like something those powdered wigs in Engineering would say.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: But you've gotta face up to a very real problem.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: If one day, Device #9 starts to malfunction, or just stops working altogether, what are you gonna do?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: I haven't seen the whole report, but Silence said something about Device #9 being necessary to keep you alive.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Regular physical examination is necessary.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: This isn't something that physical exams are gonna solve. It's a matter of life or death for you!

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Acknowledged.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Maybe I shouldn't be the one saying this but... you should really...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: You really aren't going to ask Rhodes Island for help?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Why don't you go see Closure? She's the most extraordinary engineer I've met in all my years.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Thank you for your concern, Mayer.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: This question will be revisited pending future considerations.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Sigh...
Another deep dream.
In the dream, Joyce stands in a patch of dense fog, with a soft whispering in her ear.
She cannot understand what is being whispered. It is in a language she has never heard before.
It is almost inaudible, seemingly coming from a very distant place.
She wanders through the fog and continues to dream.
Light seems to filter in from a distance, piercing the fog and illuminating the surroundings.
She sees a large Originium crystal that gives off a peculiar glow.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: So far, all your key physiological indicators are normal.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But the quality of your sleep is still poor. Are you still having those dreams through the whole night?

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: That's not a good sign. You've been in this state for too long.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: The physiological indicators are not abnormal.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Current physiological indicators can never be used to rule out problems, and you should be well aware of that. If you are unable to rest, it will become life-threatening, in the long run.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Maybe we should consult Dr. Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I'm sure she knows some way of relieving your mental burden.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Rejected. Device #9 is a confidential Rhine Lab experimental project.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: They might not even care about that project anymore.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Miss Dellareed's team has long been disbanded.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: You might be... No, you are the only legacy of the Device #9 project.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Dr. Silence, do you believe in that saying?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: To which saying are you referring?

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: 'Originium stores the story of this world, spanning hundreds or thousands of years, maybe even more.'

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: When I was with Rhine Lab, I didn't actually understand Miss Dellareed's project...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I can't answer that question. It's outside the scope of my expertise.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But the feedback data I've gotten from the monitor suggests your dreams are a side effect of Device #9.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: It might be reconstructing fragments of information you received when awake, and then playing them back repeatedly during your sleep.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: This 'playback' is one of the side effects of Device #9, in the same vein as the strong logical thinking it has brought you.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Device #9 forces your brain to stay in a continuously stimulated state, which is also the source of your poor sleep quality as well as your 'narcolepsy.'

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: As you know, Miss Dellareed's project was also full of holes. Most of the fundamental stipulations were built upon conjectures, and lacked evidentiary support.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: The basic principles of the experiment lacked solid ground, but they still had Miss Dellareed carry out that experiment. That's why you became what you are now.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Internally at Rhine Lab, the experiment was considered a failure, and that led you to...

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Objection. Erroneous account of events.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Della is not responsible for the lack of critical information in passing down that judgment.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I wasn't accusing Dellareed of...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Della? Is that what you called her?

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I know that Miss Dellareed was your friend.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Her death... had nothing to do with you. I don't have any right to blame her, but that tragedy was brought about by her obsession with her research.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I've seen... far too many tragedies like that in Rhine Lab.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Well, if it really is because of Miss Dellareed, I'm willing to have a chat with you. I'm sure Mayer would too.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: But I wouldn't fixate too much on that saying.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: And don't always bottle things up either.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Staying in a prolonged state of mental agitation won't do any favors for your health.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Right now, you are my assistant, as well as my friend. And as a friend...

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I hope that you can live a better life.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Sorry for worrying you, Dr. Silence.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Re-registering relationship status with Dr. Silence––

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: ––Friend.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: If you're in a good enough mood to be cracking jokes, I probably don't have anything to worry about.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Having that said, I'll be heading out to do some field work with Dr. Kal'tsit next week. I'm not comfortable leaving you alone in your current state.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: In other words, if you encounter any abnormalities of any kind on the way back, you must be sure to let me know.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Thank you, Dr. Silence.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Oh right, if it's not too much trouble, I'm going to ask you to take this medicine back to Ifrit.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I might run a bit late tonight.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: No problem, Dr. Silence.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: I'm bored! When is Silence getting here?

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: She's real busy today, so I came in her place.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Boo... I thought I wouldn't have to do my homework if Silence wasn't coming around.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: You lazy bum. You'd better watch yourself or Silence will make you sit down with the Doctor 'til you finish all your homework.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Naw, you ain't fooling me with that. The Doctor's even busier than Silence. Swung by the office a couple times, and nobody was there.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: That is true...

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Oh, it's Silence!

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Negative.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: It's Joyce!

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Is Silence working overtime again?

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: This is Ifrit's medicine.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Yuck... It's the bitter kind again...

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Go set it over there. I'll put it away later.

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: This is a snack for Ifrit.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Woohoo! You're the best, Joyce!

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Hold up! No snacks 'til you're done with your homework!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Fine, fine, I'm doing it!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: I got 70 points on my test today too!

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Hard work begets success. Please keep it up.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: You only got a 70, and I didn't even bust out any hard questions. Better step up your game, Ifrit.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Whatever...

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Oh, by the way...

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Why are you in such a good mood today, Joyce?

steps.name: Ptilopsis
steps.text: Some positive developments occurred. But not to the extent of necessitating a display of mood swings.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: Wait a sec, Ifrit, how'd you know that Joyce was in a good mood?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Huh? Isn't it obvious? When she's happy, her eyebrows go up a little bit, her forehead is more relaxed, and the corners of her mouth change too.

steps.name: Mayer
steps.text: How'd you figure that out?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: It's just something you get used to!

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: June 23rd, cloudy

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: Dr. Silence told me that I am her friend. I am very thankful to her.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: Dr. Silence is a good person, but because of that, I don't want to make her life harder.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: She already carries too many burdens.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: Such as Ifrit's 'Diαbolic Crisis.' And the other problems she and Saria have to face.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: But... if my fate is already sealed...

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: I hope Dr. Silence and Ifrit will have happy endings.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: My problems are very different from theirs, but they probably all stem from Rhine Lab's experiments.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: There are a lot of people like us at Rhine Lab.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: Outsiders think Columbian scientific research involves a lot of human experimentation.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: But that statement needs an addendum to be accurate. Many researchers are far too eager to carry out these experiments on themselves.

steps.name: Diary
steps.text: ...and only a tiny number of them have happy endings.
A dream––
Joyce's dream is full of hallucinations and whispers, an illusory world full of things she does not understand.
She treks through these lengthy dreams day after day, and even if she doesn't understand them, these scenes have already become commonplace.
However, during this brief moment, she suddenly realizes that the dreamscape is becoming clearer.
The wending whispers by her ear turn to recognizable words and sentences.
The mist obscuring her vision is slowly dissipating as well.
She stands atop a lofty mountain, and gazes down at everything before her.
In front of her, a magnificent city collapses into a dazzling display of metallic dust. Towering steel structures melt like clay.
In front of her, the shadow of a terrible colossus floats in the clouds above, the writhing darkness blotting out the sun and enveloping all.
In front of her, anguished screams and desperate cries waft up from the city.
Behind her, the Originium crystal shines with a peculiar glow.
